Subject: Capacity term amendment — EvoThera (proposal)

Hi team,

Quick summary: EvoThera is asking for a short-term change to their Dedicated capacity contract so they can run an experimental H100 workload for a major bench run next quarter. Key asks from EvoThera:
- Allow substitution of a portion of their committed A100 pool for H100 variants (approx 18% of committed vGPU hours) for a transient window (target 6 weeks).
- Approve a graduated overage rate schedule rather than immediate full overage — roughly 0.5x for week 1-2, 0.75x for week 3-4, 1.0x thereafter up to week 6.
- Provide a one-time bill-smoothing credit equal to 20% of the incremental consumption for month 1 to reduce their spike impact.

Why this is important: EvoThera is evaluating a performance-led product feature; H100 materially improves their run-times and reduces inference costs in their prod pipeline. If we can support a controlled transient swap and smoothing, they’ve signaled willingness to commit to an expanded committed seat after the experiment (volume upside).

Attachments: EvoThera_Dedicated_Quote_v3.pdf (quote), MAP_v2.xlsx (mutual action plan).

Requesting: Exec approval for the H100 substitution window and the staged overage schedule + bill-smoothing credit. I’ve marked approximate P&L impact in the quote but need sign-off on:
- Allowing H100 substitution for up to 6 weeks for up to 18% of committed vGPU hours.
- Temporary graduated overage schedule as outlined above.
- One-time 20% smoothing credit for month 1 of the transient window.

If approved I’ll loop Legal to push the redline (simple amendment) and Finance to create a temporary billing schedule.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference

Diego — thanks for the summary and the docs. A few quick clarifying questions before I escalate to Laura for final sign-off:
1) Can you provide expected incremental margin impact (absolute $ delta) across the 6-week window with the proposed slope? The quote has percentages but Finance needs an absolute run-rate delta.
2) Do we have evidence from infra that H100 substitution is technically compatible with their Dedicated pool and won’t require infra-side rebalancing beyond a planned maintenance window? If there’s any preemption or scheduling risk we should call it out.
3) Does EvoThera accept a firm 8-week notice to revert or extend? Their acceptance here will determine whether we structure the amendment as a time-limited swap vs open-ended.

I’m fine with the staged overage schedule in principle; the 20% smoothing credit seems reasonable if we cap the total credit exposure to $X (Finance to quantify). Please attach a one-line P&L table.

Karthik

Redwood Inference
